FOURIER ENTROPY OF THRESHOLD FUNCTIONS AND THEIR
                                              COMPOSITIONS

                                                        YITZCHAK SHMALO

     Abstract. We prove the Fourier entropy­influence inequality for every linear threshold function,
     with a constant below 8.937 and no restrictions on its weights or threshold. The argument applies
     to regular Boolean functions and gives logarithmic bounds for their Boolean combinations and for

unions with bounded variable overlap. Character multiplication preserves the estimates and yields
     bounds by influence minus variance. Under arbitrary product measures, symmetric thresholds satisfy
     the strengthened inequality needed for read-once composition, uniformly in depth and fan-in. A
     joint description of each Fourier set refines the overlap estimate and recovers constant bounds for
     addressing. Exact selector identities extend the bound to orthogonal multiplexers with shared data.
     Rare activation preserves the optimal constant of unrestricted FEI. The proofs combine pivotal
     antichains, spectral reference measures, and product-measure composition.
